cards.explanation: Paul calls himself the prisoner of Christ Jesus. Paul, the writer of this letter, says, “…I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles...” (Ephesians 3:1). Most of us lead with a job title, friends. I'd print "Master Stamper" on my business card in gold ink and hand out fifty of them. Paul leads with prisoner, and he says it's for the sake of the Gentiles.

The answer is by revelation. Paul writes, “…the mystery made known to me by revelation…” (Ephesians 3:3). Made known to him. That means it was shown to him, not dug up by him. I've read a lot of recipe cards in my day, and not one of them ever arrived by revelation.

The answer is True. Paul says it right there: “…as I have already written briefly.” (Ephesians 3:3). So this isn't the first time he's brought it up. He's circling back to it. I do the same thing with a good dough recipe, and I only wrote mine on the back of a flour sack.

The answer is God's holy apostles and prophets. Paul says it has “…now been revealed by the Spirit to God’s holy apostles and prophets.” (Ephesians 3:5). The Spirit is the One doing the revealing. Notice that it says holy apostles and prophets, so Paul is not the only one in the picture.

The answer is that they are fellow heirs in Christ Jesus. Paul says the Gentiles “…are fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus.” (Ephesians 3:6). Heirs, friends. A guest eats one cookie and heads home, but an heir shares in what's been handed down. That's what Paul is saying about the Gentiles.

The answer is False. Paul says the Gentiles are “…fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus.” (Ephesians 3:6). Fellow partakers, so they share in it with everyone else. Not one word about a smaller share.

The answer is grace. Paul writes, “I became a servant of this gospel by the gift of God’s grace…” (Ephesians 3:7). A gift, friends. He doesn't say he earned the job. The work came to him as grace, given through the working of God's power.
The answer is False. Paul says, “Though I am less than the least of all the saints...” (Ephesians 3:8). He's not at the top of that list. I think that's the humblest résumé line ever written.

The answer is the unsearchable riches of Christ. Paul says he was given grace “to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ…” (Ephesians 3:8). Unsearchable, friends. That means you can't reach the bottom of them. I've tried to reach the bottom of a cookie jar, and even that has an end.

The answer is in God who created all things. Paul says it “…for ages past was kept hidden in God, who created all things.” (Ephesians 3:9). It was hidden in God, friends. Now Paul's job is to shine a light on it. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I'll tell you, a light is a lot better than the dark.

The answer is the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms. Paul says, “His purpose was that now, through the church, the manifold wisdom of God should be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms…” (Ephesians 3:10). The heavenly realms, friends. Think about that. The church is how that wisdom gets made known to them.

The answer is True. Paul says it was “…the eternal purpose that He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.” (Ephesians 3:11). Eternal, friends. God didn't just have this purpose, He accomplished it in Christ Jesus. That's worth celebrating, and I'd say it's worth a whole batch of cookies.

The answer is False. Paul says, “In Him and through faith in Him we may enter God’s presence with boldness and confidence.” (Ephesians 3:12). The way in is through Christ and through faith in Him. Boldness and confidence are the words he picks.

The answer is that he asks them not to be discouraged by his sufferings. Paul says, “So I ask you not to be discouraged because of my sufferings for you, which are your glory.” (Ephesians 3:13). That's his request, friends. I think it's a tender thing to ask. He's the one in a hard spot, and I think he's still thinking about them.

The answer is True. Paul says it right at the end of the verse: “…my sufferings for you, which are your glory.” (Ephesians 3:13). Your glory, friends. I won't pretend to explain more than he does there. I'll just say he said it, and I think he said it kindly.
